drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/score_frame_labels.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Labels)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Score the size labels in p.json against my own labels and tell me how often the small model agrees with me and whether it beats always saying wide."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"score_frame_labels":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:score-small-model-labels-against-my-labels"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/score_frame_labels.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.
5. Read agree per field, top_confusions, agree_when_answered at each threshold, and the majority-baseline line: a model is worth wiring only when it beats the baseline.

worked_examples.title: A decider that agrees on 2 of 3 sizes, level with the majority baseline
worked_examples.ask: Score this decider's size labels against my own labels.
worked_examples.given: From tools/benchmark-small-local-models/test/test_benchmark.py (Labels.test_scores_agreement_confusions_lines_centered_and_baseline), size field only. request.json = {"shots":[{"frame":"x","w":1920,"h":1080,"reference":{"size":"wide"}},{"frame":"x","w":1080,"h":1920,"reference":{"size":"close"}},{"frame":"x","w":1080,"h":1080,"reference":{"size":"close; wide"}},{"frame":"x","w":1920,"h":1080,"reference":{"size":"unknown"}}],"vocabulary":{"size":{"wide":"w","close":"c"}},"labels":["p.json"],"reference_name":"labeller","unknown":"unknown","list_separator":";","thresholds":[0.7,0.9]} where p.json is the file a label step wrote: tag dec, rows i 0..3 with size|defined wide, wide, wide, close and confidences 0.9, 0.6, 0.95, 0.5. Run: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/score_frame_labels.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"dec|defined":{"meta":{"tag":"dec"},"fields":{"size":{"n":3,"agree":0.667,"top_confusions":["labeller close -> wide x1"],"t0.7":{"answered":0.667,"agree_when_answered":1.0},"t0.9":{"answered":0.667,"agree_when_answered":1.0},"mean_conf":0.817}}},"majority-baseline":{"fields":{"size":{"agree":0.667,"value":"wide"}}}}}: the shot labelled unknown is left out (n 3), the model agrees on 2 of 3 (0.667), the one mix-up is your close called wide, and always answering wide scores the same 0.667, so it has not beaten the baseline.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
